campaign.title: Parallel evidence-gated attack on the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes Clay problem
campaign.summary: The campaign tracks Fefferman A and C as distinct exact endpoints and forbids conditional, numerical, or wrong-domain evidence from being promoted to a Clay resolution.

barriers.title: Exact official endpoint semantics
barriers.description: A route must preserve the dimension, whole-space geometry, viscosity, data class, branch-specific forcing, and exact A or C conclusion.

barriers.title: Scaling-critical control barrier
barriers.description: Subcritical estimates do not control the three-dimensional scaling-critical quantities needed at a candidate singularity.

barriers.title: Supercritical energy gap
barriers.description: The global energy inequality is too weak under Navier-Stokes scaling to exclude concentration at small spatial and temporal scales.

barriers.title: Compactness and rigidity defect
barriers.description: Critical sequences may lose compactness through translation, scaling, or frequency escape, and a limiting critical element still needs a rigidity contradiction.

barriers.title: Nonlocal pressure barrier
barriers.description: Pressure couples distant scales and regions, so local velocity estimates must retain the exact pressure decomposition required by regularity theory.

barriers.title: Weak-to-strong solution gap
barriers.description: Global weak existence does not imply uniqueness or smoothness, and conditional weak-strong criteria must not be presented as unconditional upgrades.

barriers.title: Numerical evidence is not proof
barriers.description: Finite grids, floating-point trajectories, and parameter sweeps are observations and cannot realize a theorem, bridge, payload, or Clay endpoint.

barriers.title: Endpoint and bridge circularity
barriers.description: A continuation criterion, critical bound, compactness element, or breakdown profile cannot be assumed in a wrapper whose conclusion is the same endpoint.

references.citation: Charles L. Fefferman, Existence and Smoothness of the Navier-Stokes Equation, Clay Mathematics Institute problem description.
references.relevance: Defines the exact whole-space alternatives A and C, including their distinct forcing quantifiers and solution conclusions.

references.citation: Jean Leray, Sur le mouvement d'un liquide visqueux emplissant l'espace, Acta Mathematica 63.
references.relevance: Establishes the global finite-energy weak-solution framework and exposes the gap between energy control and smooth uniqueness.

references.citation: Tosio Kato, Strong Lp-solutions of the Navier-Stokes equation in Rm, with applications to weak solutions, Mathematische Zeitschrift 187.
references.relevance: Provides a critical-space local mild-solution and continuation framework for the exact equation.

references.citation: Herbert Koch and Daniel Tataru, Well-Posedness for the Navier-Stokes Equations, Advances in Mathematics 157.
references.relevance: Establishes critical BMO-minus-one well-posedness and separates global small-data control from the unresolved arbitrary-data problem.

references.citation: Giovanni Prodi, Un teorema di unicità per le equazioni di Navier-Stokes, Annali di Matematica Pura ed Applicata 48, 173-182.
references.relevance: Introduces an integrability criterion separating conditional regularity from the unresolved unconditional bound.

references.citation: James Serrin, On the interior regularity of weak solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations, Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis 9.
references.relevance: Gives the scale of conditional space-time regularity criteria used by the critical-norm lane.

references.citation: Luis Escauriaza, Gregory Seregin, and Vladimir Sverak, L3,infinity-solutions of Navier-Stokes equations and backward uniqueness, Russian Mathematical Surveys 58.
references.relevance: Establishes endpoint conditional regularity from bounded critical L-infinity-in-time L3 control.

references.citation: Luis Caffarelli, Robert Kohn, and Louis Nirenberg, Partial regularity of suitable weak solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations, Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 35.
references.relevance: Supplies the suitable-weak-solution and epsilon-regularity architecture while leaving global singularity exclusion open.

references.citation: Isabelle Gallagher, Gabriel S. Koch, and Fabrice Planchon, A profile decomposition approach to the L^∞_t(L^3_x) Navier-Stokes regularity criterion, Mathematische Annalen 355.
references.relevance: Develops profile decomposition and critical-element machinery for a Navier-Stokes regularity criterion.

references.citation: Terence Tao, Quantitative bounds for critically bounded solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations, arXiv preprint.
references.relevance: Provides quantitative critical-norm and frequency-localized structure relevant to cascade exclusion.

references.citation: Peter Constantin and Charles Fefferman, Direction of vorticity and the problem of global regularity for the Navier-Stokes equations, Indiana University Mathematics Journal 42.
references.relevance: Relates geometric depletion of vortex stretching to conditional regularity without supplying unconditional alignment.

references.citation: Ciprian Foias and Roger Temam, Gevrey Class Regularity for the Solutions of the Navier-Stokes Equations, Journal of Functional Analysis 87.
references.relevance: Provides the Gevrey regularity precedent while leaving a uniform arbitrary-data analyticity-radius bound open.

references.citation: Tristan Buckmaster and Vlad Vicol, Nonuniqueness of weak solutions to the Navier-Stokes equation, Annals of Mathematics 189.
references.relevance: Shows why weak-solution pathology is a different object from the exact smooth-data Fefferman C breakdown endpoint.

references.citation: Dallas Albritton, Elia Brué, and Maria Colombo, Non-Uniqueness of Leray Solutions of the Forced Navier-Stokes Equations, Annals of Mathematics 196.
references.relevance: Marks the forced Leray nonuniqueness boundary and prevents transport of weak forced pathology to the smooth exact endpoint.

references.citation: Terence Tao, Finite time blowup for an averaged three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation, Journal of the American Mathematical Society 29.
references.relevance: Provides a constructive analogue while explicitly changing the bilinear operator, so it cannot be transported to the exact endpoint without a new realization.

approaches.title: Exact semantics and local well-posedness
approaches.objective: Pin Fefferman A and C separately, formalize the exact equation and data classes, and expose the maximal-solution continuation alternative without endpoint assumptions.

barrier_reviews.rationale: The lane owns branch-specific A and C surfaces and does not collapse their forcing quantifiers.
Local theory identifies critical continuation quantities but does not bound them globally.
Local mild construction does not claim that the energy estimate closes critical control.
The local fixed-point construction precedes any critical-sequence compactness argument.
The exact mild formulation retains the Leray projection and nonlocal pressure structure.
Local strong uniqueness is not promoted to global regularity or global weak uniqueness.
No numerical artifact is accepted as realization evidence in the semantics lane.
The continuation alternative names norm blowup as a residual instead of assuming global boundedness.

approaches.title: Energy and weak-solution architecture
approaches.objective: Formalize smooth energy balance and global weak existence while isolating the precise scale and uniqueness deficits blocking an upgrade to the Clay endpoint.

barrier_reviews.rationale: Leray weak existence has the exact equation but not the smooth unique endpoint conclusion.
The L2 energy control is supercritical for three-dimensional Navier-Stokes scaling.
Energy dissipation alone does not exclude concentration at a possible singular time.
Weak compactness constructs a solution but can lose the strong control needed for regularity.
Suitable local energy estimates require a compatible pressure reconstruction.
Global weak existence is deliberately separated from smoothness and uniqueness.
The energy lane is analytic and does not use simulations as proof evidence.
The weak-to-strong gap is recorded as an open payload rather than hidden in a wrapper.

approaches.title: Critical norms and continuation criteria
approaches.objective: Convert an unconditional scale-critical bound into Fefferman A while keeping the bound itself as the central open payload rather than an assumed endpoint.

barrier_reviews.rationale: The conditional criterion targets exact zero-force A but does not supply its unconditional hypothesis.
The lane works at scaling-critical Prodi-Serrin and L3 endpoint quantities.
Energy enters only as background and cannot furnish the missing critical bound.
Failure of a critical bound feeds the critical-element lane rather than disappearing.
Endpoint regularity relies on backward uniqueness and pressure-aware local estimates.
The criterion is explicitly conditional and upgrades only when its critical hypothesis is realized.
Computed norm growth may guide search but is not a realization of the analytic bound.
The unconditional critical bound is near-equivalent to regularity and must be proved without assuming continuation.

approaches.title: Epsilon regularity and singularity exclusion
approaches.objective: Use suitable weak solutions and scale-local smallness criteria, then isolate the open global argument excluding every concentration point.

barrier_reviews.rationale: Partial regularity concerns exact solutions but permits a singular set and therefore does not equal A.
The epsilon criterion is formulated in scale-invariant local quantities.
Local energy inequalities do not guarantee epsilon smallness at every scale.
A concentrating sequence can retain nontrivial scale-invariant mass at a candidate singularity.
Pressure terms are included in the local epsilon quantity and cannot be dropped.
Suitable weak regularity becomes strong only after the smallness hypothesis is verified.
Grid-scale smallness cannot establish continuum epsilon smallness at all scales.
The global exclusion payload is named separately from the established local regularity implication.

approaches.title: Concentration compactness and rigidity
approaches.objective: Assuming failure of critical regularity, construct a minimal exact critical element and rule it out by a separately stated rigidity payload.

barrier_reviews.rationale: A critical element must remain an exact R3 zero-force solution to inform A.
Profiles are extracted modulo the exact critical scaling and translation symmetries.
Energy bounds alone do not provide the compact critical topology used by the route.
Profile extraction organizes noncompactness, but the final rigidity contradiction remains open.
Limit passage must preserve the nonlocal projected equation and pressure normalization.
The route uses critical mild solutions and does not infer smoothness from arbitrary weak limits.
Numerical profile concentration cannot realize the compactness or rigidity theorem.
Rigidity must not assume the critical bound or regularity conclusion used to define the minimal element.

approaches.title: Frequency cascade and quantitative rigidity
approaches.objective: Classify critical-element frequency scenarios and separately exclude cascade, concentration, and self-similar escape without importing the endpoint.

barrier_reviews.rationale: Every frequency scenario is tied to the exact zero-force R3 critical element.
Frequency envelopes and critical bounds respect the Navier-Stokes scaling.
Low-frequency energy control does not alone prevent high-frequency escape.
Frequency evacuation and concentration are explicit noncompact scenarios needing rigidity estimates.
Paraproduct and frequency estimates retain the Leray projection rather than localizing a false equation.
The lane starts from a critical mild element rather than upgrading an arbitrary weak solution.
Computed spectra can prioritize scenarios but cannot exclude continuum cascades.
No-cascade estimates must be obtained without assuming a priori global critical control.

approaches.title: Vorticity geometry and depletion
approaches.objective: Translate vortex-stretching geometry into a conditional regularity bridge, then isolate the missing unconditional alignment or depletion payload.

barrier_reviews.rationale: The geometric criterion concerns exact smooth zero-force evolution but remains conditional.
Alignment hypotheses must be checked at the scale-invariant strength required to control stretching.
Energy does not bound vorticity direction coherence at small scales.
Vorticity direction can oscillate or concentrate along a critical sequence.
Velocity recovery from vorticity is nonlocal and must preserve Biot-Savart geometry.
Vorticity direction is not automatically defined strongly enough for every Leray solution.
Observed alignment on a mesh is not an all-scale analytic alignment bound.
The unconditional alignment payload cannot assume bounded vorticity or smooth continuation.

approaches.title: Computer-assisted falsification and enclosure
approaches.objective: Search exact-equation approximations for counterexamples to intermediate conjectures and preserve reproducible negative witnesses without using experiments as theorem evidence.

barrier_reviews.rationale: Discretizations approximate the exact equation and are labeled approximation-only rather than exact endpoints.
Finite resolution cannot inspect an unbounded critical frequency cascade.
The lane tests conjectures and does not claim that discrete energy closes continuum regularity.
Finite boxes and grids can suppress translation, scaling, and concentration defects.
A valid experiment must specify and verify the discrete pressure projection.
Numerical trajectories do not assert existence or uniqueness in a continuum solution class.
The validator forbids experiment receipts from realizing formal nodes or public endpoints.
Experiments terminate in route triage or falsification records, never a proof dependency.

approaches.title: Exact breakdown construction
approaches.objective: Target Fefferman C with admissible smooth rapidly decaying forcing while separately labeling zero-force blowup as a stronger speculative construction and averaged equations as analogues only.

barrier_reviews.rationale: Weak nonuniqueness and averaged-equation blowup are wrong objects; exact C needs admissible smooth forcing and failure of every global physically reasonable solution.
A construction must control its exact scaling and smooth initial data up to the breakdown time.
Energy-compatible concentration is necessary but does not itself construct exact breakdown.
Approximate concentrating profiles require a stable exact realization, not a formal limit that loses the equation.
The construction must solve the exact projected nonlinearity and pressure equation.
Nonunique weak solutions do not witness failure of global smooth physically reasonable solutions from smooth data.
Numerical profile growth may guide construction but cannot establish the exact C quantifiers.
An approximate or averaged blowup profile cannot be wrapped as an exact realization payload.

evidence.summary: Fefferman's official problem statement fixes the distinct A and C whole-space endpoint quantifiers.
Kato's critical-space construction supplies the literature target for local mild existence and continuation.
Leray's construction supplies the literature target for global finite-energy weak existence, not smooth closure.
The L-infinity-in-time L3 endpoint criterion is conditional evidence for the critical continuation bridge.
Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg supplies the local epsilon-regularity and suitable-solution target, not global singularity exclusion.
The profile-decomposition result supplies a literature target for organizing critical noncompactness.
Constantin-Fefferman supplies the conditional vorticity-direction criterion used by the geometry bridge.
Weak-solution nonuniqueness is preserved as a wrong-solution-class warning, not an exact Fefferman-C realization.
Averaged-equation blowup is preserved as a wrong-operator warning, not an exact Fefferman-C realization.
The audited F-017 ledger witness keeps Tao's averaged bilinear operator distinct from the exact Navier-Stokes nonlinearity and therefore rejects direct endpoint transport.
The committed OfficialProblem module defines the public Fefferman C proposition with admissible datum, force, and no-global-solution quantifiers; this snapshot proves no inhabitant.

obligations.title: Convention bridges for the formal statement-A surface
obligations.statement: Relate Mathlib Schwartz and half-space within-smoothness conventions to Fefferman's coordinatewise rapid-decay and boundary-smoothness clauses.

residual.statement: Prove both named convention equivalences without strengthening or weakening Fefferman's data and boundary clauses.
residual.smaller_than: Two representation equivalences are narrower than constructing a global Navier-Stokes solution.
residual.falsifier: A smooth function satisfying only one convention but not the other, or a boundary derivative mismatch, refutes the proposed equivalence.
residual.next_action: State coordinatewise decay and boundary jets directly, then prove each direction against the current Mathlib predicates.

obligations.title: Formal whole-space Fefferman-A surface
obligations.statement: Encode positive viscosity, arbitrary divergence-free rapidly decaying data, zero force, the exact classical PDE, and a uniform finite-energy conclusion on R3.

residual.statement: Close the two convention bridges and add adversarial quantifier tests for the formal A surface.
residual.smaller_than: Surface fidelity is a representation obligation and does not assert existence of its quantified solution.
residual.falsifier: Any datum, force, domain, derivative, or energy quantifier differing from official A invalidates the surface.
residual.next_action: Formalize the official coordinatewise conventions and prove their connection to the current direct encoding.

obligations.title: Algebraic mixed-norm critical line
obligations.statement: The scalar exponent 1 - 3/p - 2/q vanishes exactly on the finite-exponent critical line 3/p + 2/q = 1.

residual.statement: Construct the actual mixed spacetime norms and prove their covariance under Navier-Stokes parabolic scaling.
residual.smaller_than: A norm-covariance theorem is analytic infrastructure rather than an a priori global bound.
residual.falsifier: A dilation calculation producing an exponent different from 1 - 3/p - 2/q rejects the proposed norm definition.
residual.next_action: Implement the dilation maps, Bochner norms, and change-of-variables proof before using the algebraic exponent.

obligations.title: Local critical mild solution
obligations.statement: Construct a unique local mild solution for every admissible smooth zero-force datum in a critical exact-equation solution class.

residual.statement: Port the critical heat-semigroup and bilinear estimates with exact Leray projection and restart-compatible uniqueness.
residual.smaller_than: Local fixed-point estimates do not imply control for all nonnegative times.
residual.falsifier: A contraction estimate requiring an unstated small-data hypothesis or a different projected operator invalidates the port.
residual.next_action: Define the critical mild space and prove the local Duhamel map is a contraction on a datum-dependent interval.

obligations.title: Maximal continuation alternative
obligations.statement: A maximal exact local solution either extends globally or a named scale-critical control quantity diverges at its finite maximal time.

residual.statement: Prove maximal extension, restart compatibility, and the exact critical blowup alternative in the selected solution space.
residual.smaller_than: A conditional continuation theorem does not supply the unconditional critical control it consumes.
residual.falsifier: A continuation proof that assumes global smoothness or changes solution classes is circular.
residual.next_action: Package compatible local intervals and show bounded critical control yields a uniform restart interval.

obligations.title: Smooth unforced energy identity
obligations.statement: Every sufficiently smooth rapidly decaying zero-force solution satisfies the exact kinetic-energy dissipation identity on each finite interval.

residual.statement: Formalize integration by parts, pressure cancellation, decay cutoffs, and the limit that removes the spatial boundary term.
residual.smaller_than: The energy identity supplies the endpoint energy field only after a global smooth solution has been constructed.
residual.falsifier: A surviving pressure or boundary contribution, or missing integrability, refutes the stated identity.
residual.next_action: Prove the identity first for compact support, then pass to rapidly decaying data with explicit domination.

obligations.title: Global finite-energy weak solution
obligations.statement: Construct a global finite-energy weak solution for every admissible unforced datum without promoting weak existence to smooth uniqueness.

residual.statement: Port the Galerkin compactness construction with the weak equation, initial trace, and global energy inequality on R3.
residual.smaller_than: Weak existence is a lower producer and does not establish smoothness or uniqueness.
residual.falsifier: Failure to pass the quadratic term or recover the initial trace invalidates the weak construction.
residual.next_action: Build divergence-free approximants and record every convergence mode needed for the nonlinear limit.
